author: CNN
description:
President Trump was asked Tuesday if he will accept the midterm election results, which could mean a tough night for the GOP, “whatever happens.” Trump’s reply came with a caveat made all the more ominous by his past conduct: “I will, if they are honest elections, yeah.”

Trump’s latest hedging over an election came in a threatening context. He’s spent much of this year trying to skew the midterms in the GOP’s favor by pushing a midterm gerrymandering effort in Texas and other states and by unsuccessfully demanding Congress pass a voter registration and ID law that critics say would disenfranchise millions of citizens. And he recently ordered the Justice Department to sue to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate election if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, even though the Constitution grants a president no power to administer elections.

0:00 What Trump said when asked if he'll accept election results
0:36 David Becker, founder of the Center for Election Innovation & Research,
title: Trump says he’ll accept midterm results, with a caveat

author: CNN
description:
Israel’s official vote count is now underway. With more than 70% counted, Israel is facing potential political deadlock, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival, ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot, within reach of the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat parliament, the Knesset. 

It’ll take several days to finalize the vote count. The current projections have Netanyahu’s bloc taking 54 seats, a drop from the 68-seat coalition he led in the outgoing Knesset. His Likud party is still set to be the largest single party. 

CNN's Oren Liebermann has details on the vote count. Also, New York Times contributing opinion writer Mairav Zonszein and director of American Prosperity in the Middle East, Ruby Chen, react to the results.
